verdicts.quote: The user signs in to the development org, opens the bot from inside Salesforce, and sees a place to enter a prompt.
verdicts.missing: Which Salesforce surface hosts the bot (record page component, utility bar, app page, Flow, etc.) and what context, if any, that surface passes.

verdicts.quote: A bot request does not retrieve Salesforce business records. ... The bot does not look up that record to answer.
The record, its fields, and other business data are absent from the outbound request unless the user supplied them in the prompt.
An authenticated user without bot access is denied inference.
One Salesforce user cannot read another user's prompts or replies through the bot.
verdicts.missing: Whether and how an administrator can access users' prompts and replies.

verdicts.quote: The bot keeps the xAI credential out of user-visible output.
verdicts.missing: Where the credential is stored (Named/External Credential or protected setting) and that it never appears in code, metadata or logs.

verdicts.quote: The bot resolves a request as timed out if no completed outcome is available within 120 seconds of submission.
verdicts.missing: The binding platform governor limits (callout timeout ceiling, callouts per transaction, heap, CPU time) named with their numbers.

verdicts.quote: The bot indicates when a request is pending. Observable: Delay the Grok reply and observe a pending state before the result is available.
verdicts.missing: The mechanism by which the interface learns the reply arrived (platform event, polling, LMS, etc.).

verdicts.quote: A failed submission is not automatically resubmitted by the bot.
verdicts.missing: Idempotency guarantee that a retried or re-enqueued async job cannot post the same reply twice.

verdicts.quote: Submit a prompt while Salesforce or xAI denies processing with a reported capacity or spending restriction ... The bot reports the restriction as the reason the request could not complete.
verdicts.missing: Queue depth or concurrent-job limits and their values, and handling of a request that cannot be enqueued.

verdicts.quote: The bot indicates that the prompt was rejected. ... return an HTTP 5xx error ... The user sees a failure ... The bot reports a timeout by that boundary.
When xAI returns HTTP 429, the user sees that a usage limit was reached and can try again later. ... no further inference attempt is made for it until the user submits again.
Return partial text accompanied by a provider truncation indication. The bot identifies the reply as incomplete. ... The bot reports a timeout by that boundary.
The bot does not provide saved conversations.
verdicts.missing: Whether anything is persisted server-side and, if so, its record shape (role, text, status, timestamps, model id, usage counts).

verdicts.quote: Close the bot after a completed exchange, then reopen it. The previous exchange is not available to resume in the bot.
verdicts.missing: Retention period and removal of any stored prompts/replies, including on user deletion.

verdicts.quote: The bot does not automatically transfer Salesforce business data to xAI. ... The bot communicates the transfer of submitted text to xAI before the user submits.
Each request uses the current prompt independently of other prompts. ... The bot does not silently shorten the prompt submitted for inference.
An authorized Salesforce user asks Grok a question for the first time ... rejects a prompt containing zero non-whitespace characters ... exactly 4,000 Unicode code points passes
The administrator can select an available Grok text model.
verdicts.missing: A switch to turn the bot off org-wide (beyond per-user revocation or backout) and a way for the administrator to see failed requests.

verdicts.quote: Introducing the bot does not change a production Salesforce org.
verdicts.missing: How configuration and credentials differ per environment and the deployment method (scratch org/sandbox, metadata deployment, code-coverage requirement).

verdicts.quote: within 120 seconds of submission ... The bot indicates when a request is pending.
The bot indicates that text is required ... observe a pending state ... the user can read it in the bot without it being replaced by a service error ... The user sees a failure
Bot deployment leaves pre-existing Salesforce business data intact. ... Their effective access is unchanged. ... Its configured triggers and outcomes stay the same.
